sources.title: Ghana News Agency, Government proposes changes to public holidays (25 June 2025): Act 601's days before the amendment
sources.said: January 1; Constitution Day, January 7; Independence Day, March 6; Good Friday, April 18 and Easter Monday, April 21. The others are May Day (Workers’ Day), May 1; Founders’ Day, August 4; Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Day, September 21 and Farmers’ Day, December 5. While Christmas Day is scheduled for December 25, Boxing Day, December 26, there are Commemorative Days as African Union Day for May 25 and Republic Day for July 1.

sources.title: Ghana News Agency, Parliament restores July 1 as Republic Day holiday (25 June 2025): the Amendment Act, 2025 (Act 1142, assented and commenced 30 June 2025)
sources.said: The newly passed legislation restored July 1 as Republic Day, formally recognising the country’s transition to a republic in 1960. It also introduced a new public holiday for the Muslim community, known as Shaqq Day, to be observed a day after Eid-ul-Fitr. … The bill also repealed August 4 as Founders’ Day and reinstated September 21 as Founder’s Day in honour of Dr. Kwame Nkrumah … Further, the bill empowered the President to shift public holidays that fell on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, or Thursdays to either the preceding Friday or following Monday

sources.title: Citi Newsroom (2 January 2026), from the Ministry of the Interior's statement of 2 January 2026
sources.said: Friday, January 9, 2026, will be observed as a public holiday nationwide to mark Constitution Day. According to a statement by the Ministry of the Interior, although Constitution Day officially falls on Wednesday, January 7, the President of the Republic, John Dramani Mahama, has exercised his authority under an Executive Instrument (E.I.) to shift the public holiday to Friday.

sources.title: Ghanaian Times through AllAfrica, 2 Days Holiday Declared for Eid-Ul-Fitr and Shaqq Day Celebrations (March 2026)
sources.said: "The general public is hereby informed that Friday, March 20 and Saturday, March 21, 2026 mark Eid-Ul-Fitr and Shaqq Days, which are statutory public holidays," the minister said in a statement in Accra on Friday. He explained that since March 21 falls on a Saturday, President John Dramani Mahama has issued an Executive Instrument declaring Monday, March 23 , as an additional public holiday across the country.

sources.title: Citi Newsroom, from the Ministry of the Interior's statement of 30 March 2026
sources.said: The Ministry of Interior has declared Friday, April 3, and Monday, April 6, 2026, as statutory public holidays to mark this year’s Easter celebrations.

sources.title: Citi Newsroom, from the Ministry of the Interior's statement of 27 April 2026
sources.said: The Ministry of the Interior has declared Friday, May 1, 2026, a statutory public holiday to mark May Day, also known as Workers’ Day.

sources.title: Rainbow Radio, Interior Minister Declares Wednesday, 27 May a Public Holiday for Eid-ul-Adha (16 May 2026)
sources.said: The Ministry of the Interior has officially declared Wednesday, May 27, 2026, as a statutory public holiday across Ghana in celebration of Eid-ul-Adha. In a press release issued on Friday, May 15, 2026, the Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak (MP), advised the general public to observe the day as a national holiday.

sources.title: Ghana News Agency, Friday, July 3 declared public holiday (June 2026)
sources.said: hereby informed that Friday, July 3, 2026, marks Republic Day, which is a statutory public holiday,” it said. The statement explained that although Republic Day falls on Wednesday, July 1, 2026, President of the Republic of Ghana, by Executive Instrument (E.I.), and in accordance with Section 2 of the Public Holidays and Commemorative Days Act, 2001 (Act 601), as amended, had declared Friday, July 3, as a public holiday.

sources.title: MyJoyOnline, September 21 declared public holiday for Founder’s Day (14 September 2026)
sources.said: The Ministry of the Interior has reminded the public that Monday, September 21, 2026, will be observed as a statutory public holiday to mark Founder’s Day.

sources.title: Ghana News Agency, Sunyani to host 42nd National Farmers’ Day celebration on December 4 (2 July 2026)
sources.said: The 42nd National Farmers’ Day celebration will be held in Sunyani, Bono Region, on December 4, 2026, the Ministry of Food and Agriculture has announced.

sources.title: Ministry of the Interior, Republic of Ghana, Statutory Public Holidays and Commemorative Days in the Republic of Ghana for the Year 2026 (PDF, listed at https://mint.gov.gh/public-holidays)
sources.said: New Year's Day 1st January Thursday, observance Thursday; Constitution Day 7th January Wednesday, observance Friday; Independence Day 6th March Friday; Good Friday 3rd April Friday; Easter Monday 6th April Monday; Labour Day 1st May Friday; Eid-Ul-Fitr ***; Shaqq Day (The day immediately after Eid-Ul Fitr) ***; Eid-Ul-Adha ***; Republic Day 1st July Wednesday, observance Friday, 3rd July; Founder's Day 21st September Monday; Farmers' Day 4th December Friday; Christmas Day 25th December Friday; Boxing Day 26th December Saturday, observance Monday, 28th December. NB: *** There are no fixed dates for the Eid-Ul-Fitr, Shaqq Day and Eid-Ul-Adha because they are movable feasts. The dates for their observation are provided by the Office of the Chief Imam in the course of the year. Commemorative Days: African Union Day 25th May Monday. Note: Commemorative days would not be observed as public holidays.
